section_summary: This section documents U.S. and Allied policymaking regarding access to and dissemination of Japanese technical and scientific discoveries, including debates within SANACC, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Far Eastern Commission over foreign investigators and security safeguards. It details the adoption of Far Eastern Commission policy decision FEC-280/9 granting member governments access to pre-1946 Japanese technical processes and directives transmitting this policy to SCAP. The section also contains the transmittal and opening chapters of the August 1947 report 'Reorganization of Science and Technology in Japan' by the National Academy of Sciences Scientific Advisory Group led by Dr. Roger Adams.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive policy study recommending procedures and administrative arrangements for investigating and disseminating Japanese industrial and scientific technology.
subfiles.summary: Reviews post-surrender directives, Executive Orders, and negotiations regarding the investigation and public dissemination of Japanese scientific and technical advances. Recommends that foreign investigators from Far Eastern Commission nations operate under SCAP control, with the Publication Board handling dissemination. Emphasizes that releasing Japanese discoveries will aid European rehabilitation and prevent unilateral commercial advantage.
subfiles.title: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (SANACC 216/5)

subfiles.about: Circulates a Joint Chiefs of Staff memorandum expressing national security objections to allowing foreign investigators into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Circulates JCS memorandum SM-9515 objecting to foreign investigators in Japan on security grounds and recommending U.S. personnel collect technology.
subfiles.title: Program for Investigation of Japanese Technology (SANACC 216/6)

subfiles.about: Records a diplomatic conversation regarding Australian proposals for scientific investigations in Japan and U.S. security concerns.
subfiles.from: John M. Allison, Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Allison asked Minister Stirling for Australia to delay pressing its FEC paper while SCAP develops security safeguards for foreign scientific investigators.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Australian Paper on Scientific Investigations in Japan now before FEC

subfiles.about: Report evaluating the condition of Japanese scientific institutions and proposing reforms for democratic reorganization and economic recovery.

keywords: Reorganization of Science and Technology in Japan
subfiles.summary: Presents findings of the six-member Scientific Advisory Group chaired by Dr. Roger Adams following a summer 1947 mission to Japan. Surveys Japanese academic and industrial research, noting the dominance of imperial universities, feudal faculty structures, and war damage. Analyzes the economic collapse of postwar Japan and emphasizes the necessity of science and technology for industrial reconstruction and international trade.
subfiles.title: Reorganization of Science and Technology in Japan
